paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God sees, and God acts. The LORD told Abraham the outcry against Sodom was great (Genesis 18:20), and this chapter shows He was not ignoring it. The cities and the entire plain were destroyed (Genesis 19:24-25). That's heavy, and I'm not going to joke about it.

But look at what else the chapter says. Lot hesitated, and the men "grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters," and they led them safely out "because of the LORD's compassion for them" (Genesis 19:16). Lot was no hero in that moment, and he still got rescued by a hand that wouldn't let go. Then verse 29 says God "remembered Abraham" and brought Lot out (Genesis 19:29). I think that's what I love most here: a rescue that didn't wait for Lot to get it all together.

The warning was real too. "Do not look back," the man said (Genesis 19:17), and Lot's wife looked back (Genesis 19:26). So here's your takeaway, baker: when God says move, MOVE. Don't stall, don't bargain, don't look back over your shoulder. And hang on to this, because the One who pulled Lot out by the hand is the same One who pulled me out of a junk drawer. Abraham's story isn't over yet.
